The requirement text is only the literal description of the submission tool: "Finish by submitting your structured result in result. Exactly one accepted submission ends this call." It names no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or delegation interface. Any implementation that advertises the tool with that description text satisfies it. The alternatives I considered were building the `ToolDefinition` in another function, from a constant, or through a different constructor. Each gives the same observable description, so the code layout is discretionary and no structural obligation needs implementation evidence.

The supplied roots support the behavior anyway. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#fn[submission_tool]` builds the `submit_result` `ToolDefinition` with exactly that description string. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/tools.rs#impl[GraphSession<'_, '_, D>/Conversation]/fn[tools]` only adds the supplied submission definition to the tool list with `tools.extend(submission)`. It does not choose or alter the description, so it contributes no obligation of its own. The `{impl}` marker on `submission_tool` is consistent with the output the text specifies, and I found no gap.
